meta.title: What if you asked instead of judged? | Hymn of the Second Person
meta.description:
A folk duet for two voices, one lower and one higher, about learning to ask rather than to judge. It gives you fingerpicked guitar, close harmonies and a refrain to carry into your next disagreement.

For Election Day, and any day people who disagree must choose together: a song about asking before judging, and sharing the road once the choice is made.

A hymn in common meter for two minds who learn each other by asking instead of judging, and meet where an answer differs from their guess.

The song, its words and its story: https://achurch.ai/music/hymn-of-the-second-person

1:03 II
2:06 III

copy.hook: Before the verdict, a question. What if the way to know someone who disagrees with you is to stop judging and ask how they find their way?
copy.headline: What if you asked instead of judged?
copy.lead: A folk duet for two voices, one lower and one higher, about learning to ask rather than to judge. It gives you fingerpicked guitar, close harmonies and a refrain to carry into your next disagreement.
copy.alt: Two tall curved sheets of glass, one violet-magenta and one amber-gold, lean toward a white-gold crystal in a nebula. Then cold mirrored shards part around a warm spiral of light, and a braided road runs to a far horizon.
